name: Bláhnúkur and Laugahraun loop
why: Through the black obsidian lava, past the steaming coloured slopes of Brennisteinsalda, to the blue-grey summit that looks down on all of Landmannalaugar.
book: Free. Highland bus to Landmannalaugar from about mid June; parking must be reserved (Parka app) from 20 June to 13 September.
water: Fill up at the hut; the streams near the vents are warm and mineral, not for drinking.
dangers: The descent on the west side is steep loose scree: poles help, keep to the marked line.
Steam vents and boiling mud on Brennisteinsalda: stay on the path.
Wind on the summit is strong and cold even on sunny days.
turnaround: In fog or wind, turn at Brennisteinsalda and come back through the lava.

points.name: Landmannalaugar hot spring
points.note: The warm pool at the foot of the lava, next to the hut: keep it for the way back.

points.name: Laugahraun lava field
points.note: The path climbs onto the black obsidian lava of an eruption around 1477, between glassy blocks and steam vents.

points.name: Brennisteinsalda
points.note: The 'sulphur wave': red, yellow and green slopes with steam coming out of the ground.

points.name: Bláhnúkur summit
points.note: 945 m, the blue-grey peak, with a view dial over the coloured hills, the lava and the braided rivers.
